newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks higher, seen as growing.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks higher, seen as growing.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mostly higher on Friday and traders predicted the prices would continue to grow.
"I believe the positive trend will continue," Silvana Bozic of Metroholding brokerage told Reuters.
"But the situation is delicate now since many buyers are speculating in hope that foreign investment would increase value of their shares," she said.
* Of eight active issues six were up, one was down and one stayed flat.
* Most actively traded Zagrebacka Banka gained 10 kuna to 1,010 on volume of 7,485 shares. Its GDR issued at 10 each share fell to 19.375 from Thursday's 20.125 on Seaq International in London.
* Food processor Podravka continued its steady growth adding 5 kuna to 260 and traded 2,293 shares.
* Fully listed drugs firm Pliva edged up 50 kuna to 13,150 selling 6 shares.
* Hotelier Jadranturist was up 30 kuna to 300 with 948 shares sold.
* Confectioner Kras rose 19.5 kuna to 550 selling 270 units.
* Cable-maker Elka added 2 kuna to 195 and 20 shares were sold .
* The only loser, hotelier Laguna, edged down 5 kuna to 905 after trading mixed on volume of 52 shares.
* Another hotelier Arenaturist, flat at 100 kuna, sold 291 units.
* Turnover up at 8.7 million kuna, volume higher at 11,365.
* Central bank's exchange rate: 5.4088 = $1. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
